items.e: GIVE EAR. I have previously explained in my book that the word ha’azinu (give ear) is related to the word ozen (ear). Scripture, as it were, says incline your ear.

I have previously informed you that the Gaon says that the meaning of heavens is the angels and the meaning of the earth is the people of the earth. On the other hand, its meaning might be that the rain that comes down from heaven and the fruit which the earth produces are called to bear witness. I believe that the correct interpretation is that Moses called heaven and earth to witness because they last forever. Similarly Hear, O ye mountains (Micah 6:2) and also Joshua’s stone. Scripture there writes that the stone heard. I have hinted to you that man’s soul is intermediary between the upper and lower worlds. The soul compares all things to its body. It certainly does so when speaking to other human beings. It therefore elevates the low and lowers the high.
SHALL DROP. The word ya’arof (shall drop) is related to the word ya’arof (he will break down) in He will break down their altars (Hos. 10:2). The meaning of ya’arof (shall drop) is will come down.
MY DOCTRINE. Likchi (My doctrine) refers to that which one will take away from him. It means a lesson. Compare, lekech (doctrine) in For I give you a good doctrine (Prov. 4:2).
AS THE SMALL RAIN. I believe that se’irim (small rain) refers to light rain.

AND AS THE SHOWERS. The word revivim (showers) is related to the word rav (numerous). They are adjectives. The fact that esev (herb) is stronger than deshe (tender grass) is proof of this. Some say that se’irim (small rain) is related to sa’ar (hair). Others say that it is related to the word sa’arat (storm of) in storm of God (Jer. 30:23) even though se’irim is spelled with a sin . Similarly, the phrase ve-yista’er alav (shall come against him like a whirlwind) (Dan. 11:40), which is spelled with a sin , means the same as ve-yista’er alav spelled with a samekh . It is also possible that the word se’irim has no brother in Scripture. Our verse repeats itself for emphasis, as is the style in all prophecies. The essence of our verse is that Moses prayed that his words be like dew and rain which, as it is written, do not return unfulfilled but water the earth. The meaning of the latter is that Moses’ words should enter the hearts of those who hear them in the same way that the rain affects the earth and fructifies it and causes it to produce plants.

ASCRIBE YE GREATNESS. This is addressed to the heavens and the earth, as Scripture states, The heavens declare the glory of God (Ps. 19:2), which is to be understood in accordance with my interpretation. Similarly Let the heavens and earth praise Him (Ps. 69:35).
[THE ROCK, HIS WORK IS PERFECT.] Moses opens with this phrase to make it known that all that befell Israel did so because of their evil deeds.

The meaning of The Rock is that God, like a rock, is everlasting. Do not be amazed at this, for Scripture similarly states, The Lord…shall roar like a lion (Hos. 11:10). Scripture does this because one who speaks cannot compare God’s work to anything but His works, for everything is His work. Rock, in But God is the rock of my heart (Ps. 73:26), similarly means a support, might, and permanence. Others say that tzur (rock) is related to the word tzurah (image). Compare, tzuram (their form) in And their form shall be for the nether-world (Ps. 49:15). Its basic meaning is that God does not consist of matter, which can be molded into a form. On the contrary, He is Primary form. The first interpretation appears correct to me.

HIS WORK IS PERFECT. All the works of an artisan are incomplete because the artisan needs the assistance of one greater than he. The work of God alone is perfect. Everything is a duality except for the creator of all.

FOR ALL HIS WAYS ARE JUSTICE. His ways do not change. On the contrary, they follow one law. This is the praise of God. All those who are created change their deeds in accordance with their needs. God’s works were done for His glory, with might and wisdom. The standing still of the sun (Josh. 10:12) is no argument to the contrary because, as I explained in its place, its secret is clear, from the clause And thou, Moon in the valley of Aijalon ( Ibid. ).

A GOD OF FAITHFULNESS AND WITHOUT INIQUITY. God alone has true might, for all the might of the mighty is an “accident;” that is, it depends on outside sources. The meaning of our clause is, it is not possible that God does iniquity because He is a God of faithfulness. It is possible that ve-en avel (and without iniquity) means and without iniquity in His ways. On the other hand, it is possible that the word El (God) is to be read as if written twice.

JUST AND RIGHT IS HE. Since Scripture states shichet lo (is corruption His) (v. 5), it says a perverse people corrupted God’s righteousness. Look, God alone is right. The rightness of the right is to fix that which is crooked. The word lo (v. 5) therefore refers to what He had at first.

NO; HIS CHILDREN’S IS THE BLEMISH. Lo banav (no, his children’s) means those who say that they are not his children. Scripture similarly states, Children in whom is no faithfulness (v. 20). Its meaning is that they do not admit that God created them. Although they might profess their belief verbally, they do not believe it in their hearts. The fact that they do not fear God is proof of their lack of belief. The lamed of lo (his) serves itself and another word along with it. It is to be prefixed to the word mumam (the blemish). The meaning of lemumam is, because of their blemish, their blemish consisting in being A generation crooked and perverse .

AND PERVERSE. The meaning of u-fetaltol (and perverse) is he grows strong and triumphant in his crookedness. Compare the word naftule (wrestlings) in with mighty wrestlings (Gen. 30:8). Some say that the meaning of shichet lo (is corruption His) is, they corrupted themselves; that is, they corrupted their souls. Do not wonder that the singular lo is employed, for this is the style of the language. Can you not see that Scripture reads, Remember (zekhor) the days of old, Consider (binu) the years of many generations (v. 7). I believe that shichet lo (is corruption His) means they corrupted God; that is, they corrupted the ways of God, which are implanted in man’s mind, as well as the statutes which He commanded. Scripture, as it were, says the crooked generation that is not His children corrupted Him. This is their blemish. The verse that follows, namely, Do you thus requite the Lord , is proof that this is its interpretation. I have explained the meaning of the heh in the book entitled Moznayim .
FOOLISH. In their deeds.
AND UNWISE. In heart. Look, the entire people are totally deficient in thought and deed.
THY FATHER. Scripture states this because it earlier stated that they are not His children.
THAT HATH GOTTEN THEE. Kanekha (gotten thee) is similar to kanani (made me) in The Lord made me (Prov. 8:22).
HE…MADE THEE. Fully developed you.
AND ESTABLISHED THEE. For full development.
THE DAYS OF. Yemot (days of) and yeme (days of) are two forms. The same is the case with shenot (years of) and shene (years of).
OF OLD. Olam (of old) means the time that has past.
ASK THY FATHER. Scripture states this because it earlier said Remember . If you forgot what your fathers told you, ask them.

AND HE WILL DECLARE UNTO THEE. Ve-yaggedekha means and he will declare unto thee. Compare, netattani (thou hast given to me) in for that thou hast given to me in the Southland (Josh. 15:19). And yetzauni (are gone forth of me) in My children are gone forth of me (Jer. 10:20).
THINE ELDERS. Scripture repeats itself, for it is elegant to do so.

WHEN THE MOST HIGH GAVE TO THE NATIONS THEIR INHERITANCE. The commentaries say that the reference is to “the generation of the dispersion” when all the earth became inhabited. God at that time decreed that the land of the seven nations should belong to Israel, as this land would be large enough for them. Scripture therefore reads, According to the number of the children of Israel .

HE SET. Some say that yatzev (he set) is an infinitive. Compare the word dabber (speak) in behold, I cannot speak (Jer. 1:6). Others say that yatzev (he set) is a verb in the imperfect, employed as a perfect. It is like the word ya’asu (they made) in They made a calf in Horeb (Ps. 106:19). I believe that Ask thy father alludes to those “who understand.” The same applies to “thy elders.” The meaning of the portion of the Lord is His people is similar to which the Lord thy God hath allotted (Deut. 4:19), for every portion below has a portion above.

ACCORDING TO THE NUMBER OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL. The rabbis, of blessed memory, say that the image of our father Jacob is engraved on the throne of glory. The latter is a great secret. For the portion of the Lord is His people is proof of this. This is a very great status. God did not do this for any nation. Scripture therefore states, Do ye thus requite the Lord, O foolish people and unwise ? (v. 6), that is, a people who have fallen from their status in their foolishness. Now, this God is your father, for he created you for His glory, and as Scripture goes on to explain, he taught you as a father teaches his son.
THE LOT. Chevel (lot) means a section. Compare, chavalim (the lines) (Ps. 16:6). A section is so called because land is measured with a cord.
HE FOUND HIM. The reference is to thy father that hath gotten thee (v. 6).

The meaning of He found him is that God’s glory entered into the desert with them. Furthermore, they were like a person wandering in the wilderness, a place where no man passes, for so Scripture states. The wilderness is a waste.
A HOWLING. A place where animals such as jackals and ostriches howl, and whoever hears their voices is astonished.
HE COMPASSED HIM ABOUT. The reference is to the clouds.
HE CARED FOR HIM. By giving him the Torah.
HE KEPT HIM. From the enemies.
AS THE APPLE OF HIS EYE. I have previously explained the meaning of ishon (apple).
Scripture speaks as humans do when it says His eye. It means that God protected them from all enemies and all that lay in wait.
AS AN EAGLE THAT STIRRETH UP HER NEST. Ya’ir (stirreth up) is a transitive verb. It means He leads them from place to place.

HER YOUNG. Gozalav means her young. The word gozal (a young pigeon) in and a turtle-dove, and a young pigeon (Gen. 15:9) is similar. The word gozal , along with the term efrochim (young birds), is a general term. It is similar to the term tzippor (bird).
HOVERETH. When they journey. Yerachef (hovereth) is related to the word merachefet (hovered) (Gen. 1:2). The cloud acted similarly when Israel journeyed.

SPREADETH ABROAD HER WINGS, TAKETH THEM. As an eagle takes each and every chick and bears it on her wing, for the chick does not have the strength to fly. This is the meaning of our verse. However, the meaning of how I bore you on eagles’ wings (Ex. 19:4) is connected to and brought you unto Myself ( Ibid. ). It means that Israel went out with a high hand and came quickly to Mount Sinai. It is similar in meaning to Who are these that fly as a cloud (Is. 60:8).

THE LORD ALONE DID LEAD THEM. Adonai badad (the Lord alone) means only the Lord. Its meaning is similar to At the commandment of the Lord they encamped, and at the commandment of the Lord they journeyed (Num. 9:23). God had no associate. It is possible that the word badad (alone) refers to Israel. Compare, Lo, it is a people that shall dwell alone (Num. 23:9).
AND THERE WAS NO STRANGE GOD WITH HIM. With Israel. They roused Him to jealousy with strange gods (v. 16) is proof that this interpretation is correct.
HE MADE HIM RIDE ON THE HIGH PLACES OF THE EARTH. The land of Canaan, which is in the center of the inhabited world. He made him ride is metaphorical.

The reading of the word bamote (high places) does not change because of the vav . It is related to the word bamotemo (their high places) (Deut. 33:29). The word bemotav (with…his tomb) in the wicked … with…his tomb (Is. 53:9) is not related to our word.
FRUITAGE. The word tenuvot (fruitage) means fruit. It is related to the word yanuv (increase) in If riches increase (Ps. 62:11).

FIELD. Sadai (field) is an adjective. It follows the paradigm of chakham (wise). The yod of sadai is in place of a heh . It is similar to the vav of shalev (at ease) in I was at ease (Job 16:12). The clause ya’aloz sadai (let the field exult) (Ps. 96:12) wherein ya’aloz is in the singular proves this.

AND HE MADE HIM TO SUCK HONEY OUT OF THE CRAG. This is a metaphor. It is like That the mountains shall drop down sweet wine (Joel 4:18). The reference is to the abundance of honey and oil which, as is clearly stated in Scripture, were exported from the land of Canaan

OUT OF THE FLINTY ROCK. The lamed in chalmish (flinty) has no dagesh because the word is in the construct. Me-chalmish tzur (out of the flinty rock) is the reverse of mi-tzur ha-challamish (out of the rock of flint) (Deut. 8:15). The same is true of charvot tzurim (knives of flint) and tzur charbo (his sword of flint) (Ps. 89:44).
CURD OF KINE. An abundance of meat.

AND MILK OF SHEEP, WITH FAT OF LAMBS. Were it not for tradition then this verse would serve to support my opinion regarding the fat which I mentioned in its place. On the other hand, fat in with fat of lambs means the fleshy and the good. Compare, All the best (chelev) of the oil (Num. 18:12).
OF THE BREED OF BASHAN. Who were raised in the mountain of the Bashan.
WITH THE KIDNEY-FAT OF WHEAT. This is metaphorical, for the fat lies on the kidneys. The kernel of wheat also looks like a kidney.

AND OF THE BLOOD OF THE GRAPE. The wine. The Land of Israel thus contains an abundance of honey, oil, meat, bread, wine, and all sorts of fruit. This is the meaning of the fruitage of the field (v. 13). Some say that honey refers to date honey.
FOAMING WINE. The word chamer (foaming wine) means wine. Compare, kerem chemed (a vineyard of foaming wine) (Is. 27:2).

[THOU DRANKEST FOAMING WINE.] The tav of the word tishteh (thou drinkest) is a second person prefix. Our verse, as it were, speaks like a person who tells his friend the land has so much wine that you will drink it at all times. Some say that enav (grape) is in the feminine. However, what they say is worthless, for the tav should have been vocalized with a pattach so that it would be a causative. Some say that tishteh speaks of the community, for the word Israel is sometimes in the masculine and sometimes in the feminine. This interpretation is a bit closer to the correct meaning.

BUT JESHURUN WAXED FAT. Jeshurun refers to Israel. It is possible that the name Jeshurun is related to the word yashar (upright). Its meaning is, the one who was upright became fat. Some say that the word Jeshurun is related to the word ashurennu (I behold him) (Num. 23:9). The first interpretation appears “upright” in my eyes. The fact that Jeshurun is in the singular is proof of this.
AND KICKED. The word va-yivat (and kicked) is similar to tivatu (kick ye) in Wherefore kick ye (I Sam. 2:29). Its meaning is to be ascertained from its context.
THOU DIDST WAX FAT. It did not enter their minds to take stock of themselves.
THOU DIDST GROW THICK. The word avita (thou didst grow thick) is similar to the word avah (thicker) in My little finger is thicker (I Kings 12:10).

THOU DIDST BECOME GROSS. Some say that kasita (thou didst grow thick) is similar to kissah (he hath covered) in he hath covered his face with his fatness (Job 15:27), for the word is found in the kal conjugation. Others say that kasita is similar to ke-seh (like…a sheep) in I have gone astray like a lost sheep (Ps. 119:176). We do not find such a construction in any of the verbs. It appears to me the word kasita has no brother. Its meaning is, you kicked.
AND HE FORSOOK. The commandments of his God.

AND CONTEMNED. In mind and verbally. Its correct meaning is that Israel profaned the name of the Lord for not saving him. He caused this to be. Scripture therefore continues, the Rock of his salvation , which is to be understood as The Rock, His work is perfect (v. 4).
THEY ROUSED HIM. In their thoughts. Compare, and now nothing will he withheld from them (Gen. 11:6).
WITH STRANGE GODS. Be-zarim is to be interpreted as with strange gods.
WITH ABOMINATIONS. The reference is to idols.

DEMONS. Shedim (demons) has the same meaning as s e’irim (satyrs) in the satyrs after whom they go astray (Lev. 17:7). Therefore Rabbi Isaac the son of Saul who rests in Eden says that the word se’arum (dreaded) in Which your fathers dreaded not is related to the word se’irim . The lamed of la-shedim (unto demons) pertains to shedim and also to another word. La-shedim lo eloha (unto demons, no-gods) is to be read as if written la-shedim u-le-lo eloha (unto demons and unto no-gods). I believe that there is no need for this interpretation. On the contrary, the meaning of la-shedim lo eloha is clearly, unto demons who are no-gods. They are called shedim in the same way that the Emim are called Emim. They are called shedim because they destroy reason.

GODS THAT THEY KNEW NOT. How could Israel think that these gods were deities when they did not know these gods by proof. This is the meaning of they knew not . Neither did they know them by tradition. This is what Which your fathers dreaded not refers to.
NEW GODS THAT CAME UP OF LATE. A few days ago. They are not ancient. Even their fathers did not know them.

DREADED. Se’arum means they were not in dread of them. Se’arum is related to the word ve-yista’er (shall come like a whirlwind) in shall come against him like a whirlwind (Dan. 11:40). It is similar in meaning to sa’ar in That made the hair (sa’arat) of my flesh to stand up (Job 4:15). However, it appears that se’arum is related to the word sa’arah (storm) even though the latter is spelled with a samekh . Se’arum is similar to yetza’uni (are gone forth of me) in My children are gone forth of me (Jer. 10:20) and in chazaktani (Thou hast overcome me) in Thou hast overcome me, and hast prevailed (Jer. 20:7); that is, you are more powerful than me. Look, the meaning of se’arum is, they were not afraid of them.

OF THE ROCK THAT BEGOT THEE THOU WAST UNMINDFUL. These are the words of the prophet. He wonders: How did you forget the One who begot you? You served new gods. Also, this clause, the rock that begot thee , is similar to Look unto the rock whence ye were hewn (Is. 51:1). Israel, as it were, came from God, for everything comes from God’s might. Compare, That spread the earth by Myself (Is. 44:24). One must be amazed by those who err in their hearts because Scripture states, This day have I begotten thee (Ps. 2:7). They have forgotten this verse.

[THOU WAST UNMINDFUL.] The word teshi (thou wast unmindful) is related to the word tinnasheh (you will forget) in [the clause] you shall not forget. The missing silent letter following the tav is in place of the omitted dagesh which compensates for the first root letter, and the yod is in place of the heh . Compare the word temchi (blot out) in Neither blot out their sin (Jer. 18:23). Both words are accented penultimately in order to show a difference between the masculine and the feminine in verbs whose last letter is a silent heh . However, it appears to me that the yod is superfluous. It follows the same rule as tet (decline) does in neither decline (Prov. 4:5).

THAT BORE THEE. Mecholelekha means that bore thee. Observe, God who is powerful and mighty as a rock [gave birth to you]. It is possible that the word mecholelekha is related to the word chil (pain), as in Like as a woman with child , that draweth near the time of her delivery, Is in pain (tachil) (Is. 26:17).
AND SPURNED. Scripture similarly writes, veyanetz ha-shaked (And the almond-tree shall blossom) (Eccles. 12:5). On the other hand, it might be an intransitive verb.
HIS SONS AND HIS DAUGHTERS. Men and women, for they too sacrificed to the idols.
AND HE SAID. God in His heart or to the angels.
I WILL HIDE MY FACE. Scripture speaks as people do. Similarly I will hide Mine eyes from you (Is. 1:15). It means that when they search for Me they will not find help.

I WILL SEE WHAT THEIR END WILL BE. Some say that our verse is to be interpreted, I will hide My face from them because I see what they will ultimately do. However, it is to be understood according to its literal meaning, that is, [so that] I will see what they will do when trouble comes upon them.
FOR THEY ARE A VERY FROWARD GENERATION. This is connected to I will hide My face .

FROWARD. They turned about and served gods besides Me. They were My children, for I gave birth to them. Look, there is no faithfulness in them. The word emun (faithfulness) is a noun. On the other hand, it might be an adjective meaning there is no faithful man among them, for we find for the faithful fail (Ps. 12:2) in which faithful is parallel to godly ( Ibid. ). We also find that keepeth faithfulness (emunim) (Is. 26:2).
THEY HAVE ROUSED ME. The second root letter has no dagesh in order to simplify enunciation.
WITH A NO-GOD. Its meaning is, a god that has no power to deliver.
WITH THEIR VANITIES. Rather than with something which truly exists.
I WILL ROUSE THEM. Akni’em (I will rouse them) is a hifil . It describes two actions.

WITH A NO-PEOPLE. A nation who are not My people. Scripture describes how God shall anger them. He will bring upon Israel, upon Israel alone, unique troubles which surpass the adversity that he brought upon all others.
A VILE NATION. For a fool and a vile person lack understanding. He therefore kills and has no pity.

KINDLED. Their provocation, or that which they did, for we find the word kadechah (kindled) to be transitive, as in For ye have kindled (kedachtem) a fire in My nostril (Jer. 17:4). It is possible that kadechah means is kindled. It is like the word chaveru (came as allies) (Gen. 14:3), the meaning of which is gathered. All of this refers to God’s burning anger.
UNTO THE DEPTHS OF THE NETHER-WORLD. Its meaning is similar to that of and that the whole land thereof is brimstone, and salt, and a burning (Deut. 29:22).
AND DEVOURETH. Israel.
AND SETTETH ABLAZE. Va-telahet (and setteth ablaze) is related to the word lahat (flaming) in and the flaming sword (Gen. 3:24).
THE MOUNTAINS. The mountains of Israel.

I WILL HEAP. Some say that the word aspeh (I will heap) means I will add. However, it really means I will consume. Compare, tispeh (sweep away) in Wilt Thou indeed sweep away (Gen. 18:23). The aforementioned is so, even though aspeh and tispeh differ in conjugation. It means that there will be no evil that will not come upon them. Scripture compares the evils to arrows that suddenly appear and there is no way to guard oneself against them.
THE WASTING OF HUNGER. Meze ra’av (the wasting of hunger) means burnt by hunger. Meze (wasting) is similar to le-meze (that they should heat) in that they should heat the furnace (Dan. 3:19).

AND THE DEVOURING OF THE FIERY BOLT. Le-chume reshef (the devouring of the fiery bolt) means consumed by birds. Compare, As the birds (bene reshef) fly upward (Job 5:7). It appears to me that Scripture mentions the four evil punishments. They are: starvation , which is what The wasting of hunger refers to; and the devouring of the fiery bolt, And bitter destruction refers to the plague ; And the teeth of beasts will I send upon them refers to the beast : and finally [there is] the sword , as in Without shall the sword bereave (v. 25). Reshef (the fiery bolt) is thus similar to reshfeha rishpe esh (The flashes thereof are flashes of fire) (Cant. 8:6). It means that the air will grow hot.
AND …DESTRUCTION. Ketev means destruction.

BITTER. Meriri (bitter) refers to bitterness in the air. Compare, ke-meriri yom (like the bitterness of the day) (Job 3:5). Scripture similarly writes, Nor of the destruction (ketev) that wasteth at noonday (Ps. 91:6). The latter refers to the plague. The word u-lechume in u-lechume reshef (and the devouring of the fiery bolt) means devoured by. There are many such instances.
WITH THE VENOM OF CRAWLING THINGS OF THE DUST. The reference is to being bitten. Venom refers to being bitten.

[DUST.] This refers to fiery snakes. Zochale (crawling) is related to the word fear. They are called zochale because all who see them are afraid of them. It is similar to the term emim . This is so because there are adjectives [without nouns]. Its counterpart is found in the speech of Elihu the son of Barachel (Job 32:6).
BOTH YOUNG MAN. This is connected to Without shall the sword bereave .
Scripture reads gam (both) in accordance with the rules of the Hebrew language, as I have previously explained. Look, the Torah includes all: young men, virgins, old men, and youths.

I WOULD MAKE AN END OF THEM. Some say that the word afehem (I would make an end of them) is a combination of three words. Actually, it has no neighbor. Its meaning is, I will destroy them, for Scripture states afterwards, I would make their memory cease from among m en. Look, all of them will die. If the grammarians who say that afehem means I will scatter them to all the corners are right, then the idea expressed by the first part of the verse is not to be connected to that of the second. Some say that the meaning of afehem is, I will destroy them in my anger. Behold, the meaning of afehem is, I will destroy them. Afehem is similar in meaning to ashbitah (I would make…cease). Scripture repeats itself. This interpretation would be correct were it not for the alef of afehem , for the word should have read anfehem , meaning I will be angry at them. The first interpretation is correct.
[I THOUGHT.] The meaning of amarti (I thought) is, I said to Myself. The Torah speaks as people do.

I DREADED. Agur means I dreaded. It is related to the word va-yagar (was sore afraid) in And Moab was sore afraid (Num. 22:3). The Aramaic translation connects it to the word agerah (gathereth) in And gatherest…in the harvest (Prov. 6:8). Actually it is related to the word tigrah (fight). Scripture speaks as people do so that those who hear will understand.

SHOULD MISDEEM. Yenakkeru (misdeem) is the reverse of yakkiru (they shall recognize). Yenakkeru is similar to va-yitnakker (but made himself strange) in but made himself strange unto them (Gen. 42:7).
HATH WROUGHT ALL THIS. Upon the tribes.

FOR THEY ARE A NATION VOID OF COUNSEL. The reference is to the enemies of Israel. This is its correct interpretation. The word ovad (void) is an adjective. It is in the construct. It is therefore vocalized with a pattach beneath the bet . It is known that the word ovad is an intransitive verb. The correct interpretation of ovad etzot is that etzot (counsel) reverts to ovad (void). It is similar to novelet aleha (whose leaf fadeth) (Is. 1:30). The same is true of ve-tovedu derekh (and ye perish in the way) (Ps. 2:12) wherein tovedu is connected to derekh . The Aramaic translator who rendered ovad etzot as me’abbede etzah (void of counsel) understood this.

IF THEY WERE WISE. If they were wise and understood that God did all of this to Israel because of all their sins, they would comprehend their eventual end, namely, that God would do so because of their sins.

HOW SHOULD ONE CHASE. If Israel was wise they would understand how one of their enemies could pursue a thousand Israelites. This occurred only because their Rock has forsaken them. Others interpret our verse as how did Israel, who are now weak, at first pursue a thousand of their enemies.

EXCEPT THEIR ROCK HAD GIVEN THEM OVER. Mekharam means had given them over. The same applies to yimkor (will give over) in for the Lord will give Sisera over (Jud. 4:9). Its meaning is that God, as it were, gave them over as in payment for their deeds. It is thus a literal sale.

HAD DELIVERED THEM UP. Hisgiram (had delivered them up) is similar to yisgor (shutteth up) in, He shutteth up a man (Job 12:14). On the other hand, it might be similar to hasgiro (deliver him up) in and our part shall be to deliver him up (I Sam. 23:20).

FOR THEIR ROCK IS NOT AS OUR ROCK. These are the words of Moses. Moses explains for they are a nation void of counsel (v. 28). It means that our Rock has handed us over, and the nations have no rock like our Rock, and they are no better than we are. Scripture similarly states, and our enemies are not judges. Compare, And I have not learned wisdom (Prov. 30:3). Others say that the meaning of Even our enemies themselves being judges is as follows: our enemies admit this. It is therefore not connected to For their vine is of the vine of Sodom (v. 32).
AND OF THE FIELDS OF GOMORRAH. Scripture repeats itself. The same is true of Their clusters are bitter .
THE VENOM OF. Look, the wine is like the venom of angry serpents.

AND THE CRUEL POISON OF ASPS. Petanim (asps) is similar to the word paten (asp) in on the hole of the asp (Is. 11:8). Even though rosh (poison) is spelled with an alef , it has the same meaning as its counterparts which are spelled with a vav.
CRUEL. Akhzar (cruel) means mighty. The alef is superfluous, like the alef of etzba (finger) and ezro’a (arm).

IS NOT THIS LAID UP IN STORE WITH ME. These are the words of God. Some say the reference is to the decrees. It appears to me that the reference is to their wine, which is the poison of asps. It is laid in store until they drink it. The meaning of the word kamus (laid up in store) is to be ascertained from its context, for it has no family.
SEALED UP IN MY TREASURIES. So that no hand touches it. It is kept for them, for vengeance is to be exacted from them.

VENGEANCE IS MINE, AND RECOMPENSE. Shillem (recompense) is a noun. It is like the word kitter (offering) in The offering…did not (Jer. 44:21). It means that Vengeance is mine , and mine is the recompense to compensate them in accordance with their deeds.
AGAINST THE TIME WHEN THEIR FOOT SHALL SLIP. It means they will fall and be unable to stand.
The meaning of Against the time is similar to that of Yea, even the wicked for the day of evil (Prov. 16:4). It is a great secret.
FOR THE DAY OF THEIR CALAMITY IS AT HAND. Let them not think that the vengeance will be exacted from their children.

AND THE THINGS THAT ARE TO COME UPON THEM SHALL MAKE HASTE. Ve-chash atidot lamo (and the things that are to come upon them shall make haste) means each one of the future events that are to come upon them shall make haste. It is like Its branches (banot) run (tza’adah) over the wall (Gen. 49:22). Or the meaning of ve-chash atidot lamo is, the day ( yom ) when the future things that are to come upon them makes haste. The first interpretation is correct. The word chash (make haste) comes from a root in which only two letters are present.
The meaning of the things that are to come is, the evil things that are about to come.
FOR THE LORD WILL JUDGE HIS PEOPLE. God will exact judgment from Israel’s enemies on behalf of His people. It is like Be Thou my judge, O God, and plead my cause (Ps. 43:1).
AND REPENT HIMSELF. I have previously explained this.

THEIR STAY IS GONE. The stay of Israel. Yad (stay) means the strength. The tav of azelat is in place of a heh , for both the heh and the tav are signs of the feminine. The word ve-shavat (then it shall return) in then it shall return to the prince is similar (Ezek. 46:17).
AND THERE IS NONE REMAINING, SHUT UP OR LEFT AT LARGE. When the captives are numerous, the captors take some of them and leave others, but in this case almost all are lost.
AND IT IS SAID. And the enemy shall say.
THE ROCK IN WHOM THEY TRUSTED. This is to be understood in accordance with my previous interpretation.

WHO DID EAT. Scripture employs the language of the enemies who thought that the burnt offerings serve as food for God. Scripture employs the plural as they do. The Torah therefore states, I , only I, am He, And there is no god with Me (v. 39).

THE WINE OF THEIR DRINK-OFFERING. Yen nesikham (the wine of their drink-offering) is similar to venisko yayin (and the drink-offering thereof shall be of wine) (Lev. 23:13). They are two terms. Some say that yen nesikham (the wine of their drink-offering) means the wine of their king, for the kings used to donate the wine for the burnt offering. Compare, nesikhe midian (the princes of Midian) (Josh. 13:21). The first interpretation appears correct to me.
AND HELP YOU. Ve-yazrukhem (and help you) is similar to berakhnukhem (we bless you) (Ps. 119:26). If you say that the Lord alone is God then let Him protect you from the coming troubles.

I, EVEN I. The word I is written twice. Compare, I, even I (Is. 51:12). On the other hand, its meaning might be, I am He, and I do not change. The latter is the correct interpretation, for God has no co-worker. I am He that put Israel to death, and I will bring them back to life. Look, they were not saved. There is none that can deliver you out of My hand, even you out of My hand, until I execute My judgment upon you. Many say that we can derive the existence of life in the future world from this verse. They offer proof from the fact that Scripture first states, I kill and then, I make alive . It similarly reads, The Lord killeth, and maketh alive (I Sam. 2:6). He bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up (Ibid. ) is proof. Others offer proof from: And surely your blood of your lives (nafshotekhem) will I require (Gen. 9:5). Also from And it shall be righteousness unto us (Deut. 6:25); for that is thy life (Deut. 30:20) in the world to come, and the length of thy days (Ibid. ) in this world; that it may go well with thee (Deut. 5:16). Rabbi Hai Gaon, of blessed memory, says that Scripture had no need to state clearly that a future world exists because it was known by tradition. I believe that [Scripture does not speak of a future world] because the Torah was given to all. It was not given to an individual alone. The topic of the world to come is not comprehended by even one in a thousand, for it is very abstruse. The reward in the world to come is contingent on the nature of the soul. The reward is given for the service of the heart. The latter consists in comprehending the works of God, for they are the ladder whereon one ascends to the level of understanding the knowledge of God, which is what is most important. Observe, the Torah itself explains to the intelligent the topic of the tree of life. Behold, there is a power by which one can overcome the cherubim. The one who eats from the tree of life gains eternal life like the ministering angels. The psalm of the sons of Korah similarly reads, Hear this, all ye peoples… (Ps. 49:2). The secret is But God will redeem my soul from the power of the nether-world; For He shall receive (take) me. Selah (Ps. 49:16). Scripture similarly states, And afterward receive (take) me with glory (Ps. 73:24). Both verses employ the word “taking” as Scripture does in the account of Enoch and Elijah. Now, since Scripture states, But God will redeem my soul [ from the power of the netherworld ] (Ps. 49:16), how could it say, For too costly is the redemption of their soul (Ps. 49:9)? The intelligent will understand.

FOR I LIFT UP MY HAND TO HEAVEN. An oath taken over something which is everlasting. For I lift is similar to when he lifted up his right hand and his left hand unto heaven and swore by Him that liveth for ever (Dan. 12:7). The term I lift up is an anthropomorphism so those who hear will understand.
AS I LIVE FOR EVER. As I live so will I do this.

IF I WHET. Shannoti (I whet) comes from a double root. Compare, channoti (I am loathsome) in And I am loathsome to the children of my tribe (Job 19:17). Shannoti is related to the word shanun (sharp) in and a sharp arrow (Prov. 25:18).
AND MY HAND TAKE HOLD ON JUDGMENT. The sword is the instrument by which the warrior executes judgment.
I WILL RENDER VENGEANCE TO MINE ADVERSARIES. The meaning of ashiv (I will render) is, I will do to Mine adversaries as they did to Israel. This is also the meaning of And will recompense (ashallem).
WITH THE BLOOD OF THE SLAIN. This explains I will make Mine arrows drunk .
[THE CAPTIVES.] It means the wounded.
FROM THE…HEADS. This explains shall devour flesh . It means that the head shall be chopped off.
LONG-HAIRED. The word parot (long-haired) is similar to bi-fero’a pera’ot (When men let grow their hair) (Jud. 5:2). The rabbis also employ the term ha-nifra (one who collects).

SING ALOUD, O YE NATIONS. Then, when God avenges Israel’s blood, the nations will praise Him. Some say that the meaning of harninu (sing aloud) is similar to the word rinnah (cry) in And there went a cry (I Kings 22:36). It means the herald. Proclaim about them in every place where they are.

AND DOTH MAKE EXPIATION FOR THE LAND OF HIS PEOPLE. Some say that a vav is missing. Our verse should be interpreted as if written ve-khipper admato ve-ammo (and doth make expiation for His land and for His people). According to the midrash the meaning of ve-khipper admato ammo (and doth make expiation for His land of His people) is that the land makes expiation for His people. This interpretation is true in itself. However, it is not the meaning of the verse. Furthermore, the word adamah (land) is a feminine. The heh at its end is proof of this. The tav takes the place of the heh . Now, Scripture does not read vekhipperah (and doth make expiation). In my opinion the meaning of our clause is that the people will make expiation for the land, for we find Scripture stating, avanim shachaku mayim (The waters wear the stones) (Job 14:19). The word kippur (expiate) is also found without the word al (for), as in ve-khippartahu (and make atonement for it) in, thus shalt thou purify it and make atonement for it (Ezek. 43:20). The meaning of ve-khipper admato ammo is that Israel will execute vengeance upon the nations and they will make atonement for the Land of Israel because of the blood that was shed in it. Compare, and no expiation can be made for the land [ for the blood that is shed therein, but by the blood of him that shed it ] (Num. 35:33). This interpretation is in keeping with the meaning of the context. On the other hand, the meaning of ve-khipper (and doth make expiation) is, and will purify, as in ve-khippartahu (and make atonement for it) (Ezek. 43:20). Ezekiel similarly said, regarding the end of the wars, Thus shall they cleanse the land (Ezek. 39:16). Israel will thus purify the land.

AND MOSES CAME. Our verse teaches that after Moses went to each one of the tribes and charged them, when he came to the tent of meeting and all of the children of Israel were gathered unto him, he spoke the words of this song.

HE, AND HOSHEA THE SON OF NUN. This is similar to Then sang Moses and the children of Israel (Ex. 15:1). Also, this was done to exalt the status of Joshua in the eyes of all. Scripture refers to Joshua by the name of Hoshea because it was the name by which he was known to all of Israel, for who aside from the elect of the assembly knew that Moses referred to Hoshea by the name of Joshua. The approach of the midrash is known.
BECAUSE IT IS YOUR LIFE. Its meaning is similar to that of The fear of the Lord prolongeth days (Prov. 10:27). Furthermore, you shall be in a good land and not in exile.
THAT SELFSAME DAY. The day that he delivered the song.

AND DIE. To prepare himself for death, for Moses, as I will explain, was to bury himself. I have hinted earlier what one of the wise men of the generation said regarding the word va-ye’asef (and was gathered) (Gen. 25:8).
BECAUSE YE SANCTIFIED ME NOT. I have previously explained this.
THE LAND. This explains thither .
AND THIS IS THE BLESSING. This blessing is similar to the blessing of Jacob.
THE MAN OF GOD. This teaches that Moses blessed them prophetically.
BEFORE HIS DEATH. Close to his death. This means on the day of his death.

CAME FROM SINAI. The Gaon, of blessed memory, says that Mount Sinai, Seir, and Paran are close to each other. This verse speaks of the revelation at Sinai. Scripture reads mi-sinai (from Sinai), for mi-sinai has the same meaning as be-sinai (on Sinai). The same applies to the term mise’ir (from Seir).
FROM THE MYRIADS HOLY. The reference is to the angels. Scripture speaks of the Divine presence, which descended.

A FIERY LAW UNTO THEM. The Torah, which was given through fire and lightning. He says that the Lord came… is a prayer. It means, You who came to Sinai and bequeathed the Torah, Let Reuben live (v. 6). However, this interpretation is far-fetched, for Scripture should read, keep Reuben alive and do not put him to death. Those who lack faith say that from Seir refers to the religion of the Edomites, and Paran refers to the faith of the Ishmaelites. However, these err. Do they not see that Moses commenced at first to bless Israel alone. Scripture thus reads, wherewith Moses the man of God blessed the children of Israel (v. 1). Scripture goes on to say ve-zarach mi-se’ir lamo , the meaning of which is, And rose from Seir unto them. Compare, lamo (for them) in And there is no stumbling for them (Ps. 119:165). It appears to me that this chapter is a general blessing to all of Israel. Moses then goes on to address each tribe and tribe individually. Then Moses includes them all in the verse which reads, There is none unto God, O Jeshurun (v. 26). Look, we find that Deborah said, Lord, when Thou didst go forth out of Seir, When Thou didst march out of the field of Edom, The earth trembled (Jud. 5:4). Clearly the field of Edom is not a mountain as the Gaon says, for the Gaon maintains that Sinai, Seir, and Paran are three mountains close to each other or facing each other. Also, the Book of Psalms states, O God, when Thou wentest forth before thy people, When Thou didst march through the wilderness (yeshimon); Selah (Ps. 68:8). Scripture then states, The earth trembled (Ps. 68:9). Now the Divine presence did not march through the wilderness ( yeshimon ) on the day that the Torah was given, for Israel came to the wilderness ( yeshimon ) after they had passed through the wilderness ( midbar ) of Paran. Furthermore, Habakkuk says, God cometh from Teman (Hab. 3:3). Teman was one of the sons of Edom, for we read, Teman, Omar (Gen. 36:11). From Teman means the same as from the field of Edom . Look, all the verses speak of war. Let God arise, let His enemies be scattered (Ps. 68:2) is proof of this. Scripture describes God’s saving of His servants in terms of help coming down from heaven, the earth melting, the mountains dissolving, and the heavens quaking. Then the earth did shake and quake (Ps. 18:8) in David’s song is proof of this. I have explained the meaning of even yon Sinai (Ps. 68:9) in its place. The following is the explanation of our verse. The Lord came refers to the glory that entered into Israel. It first entered Israel at Sinai. And rose from Seir means that God did not show His might among the nations all the years that Israel was in the wilderness until Israel came to the field of Edom. Scripture similarly states, in their mount Seir, unto El-paran (Gen. 14:6). Seir and Paran are thus close to each other. The meaning of And rose from Se’ir is thus explained, for mi-seir means from the place of Seir; that is, when Israel came to Seir, God’s glory rose to Israel. He shined forth from mount Paran repeats the idea expressed by and rose from Seir . It means that God here showed His shining.

AND HE CAME FROM THE MYRIADS HOLY. I believe that this is connected to At His right hand . It means that fire came from the myriads holy at God’s right hand to surround Israel. It is similar to the horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha (II Kings 6:17).
[FIERY LAW.] The meaning of law is something constant.

YEA, HE LOVETH THE PEOPLES. Hovev (loveth) comes from an Aramaic word. It has the meaning of then ye shall be Mine own treasure from among all peoples (Ex. 19:5). The peoples refers to Israel. Compare, After thee, Benjamin, among thy peoples (Jud. 5:14); They shall call peoples unto the mountain (v. 19 ).
[ALL HIS HOLY ONES.] This refers to the sons of Levi.
THEY ARE IN THY HAND. They are round about the ark.
AND THEY SIT DOWN AT THY FEET. This means they will walk in Your ways. The meaning of in Thy hand is, you will protect them.
RECEIVING OF THY WORDS. They will teach Torah. They are the ones who transmit the oral Torah.
RECEIVING. Each and every one. This is so even though they are many.
The meaning of Thy words is, that which You spoke they will bear, for they are the bearers of the Torah, and they also carry the ark.
The word yissa (receiving) is similar to tissa (uttering) in Thou shalt not utter a false report (Ex. 23:1).

AND THEY SIT DOWN. Tukku (sit down) has no brother. Some say that it is related to the word mi-tokh (from the midst of). They, as it were, walk in the midst of Your feet. Others say that the tav is in place of a heh . It is like the tav of tirgalti (I taught) in I taught Ephraim (Hos. 11:3). The meaning of our verse is, even if they are beaten on Your account, they will not forsake Your words. However, this is farfetched. Actually it means are drawn; they go to the place of the ark which serves as the footstool for God’s feet. This is the blessing: May God be a wall of fire round about Israel. May Israel be God’s treasure. May the Levites always teach the Torah.

MOSES COMMANDED US A LAW. This is what they shall bear upon their lips and say from generation to generation: thus did we copy with our hands an inheritance from the mouth of Moses. The lamed of lanu (us) applies to itself and also to another word. Morashah kehillat ya’akov (an inheritance congregation of Jacob) should be read as if written morashah le-kehillat ya’akov (an inheritance of the congregation of Jacob). It is similar to ve-hanevu’ah oded ha-navi (even the prophecy Oded the prophet) (II Chronicles 15:8). Or morashah (an inheritance) should be read as if written twice. Our clause should be read as if written an inheritance, an inheritance of the congregation of Jacob.

A KING. The reference is to Moses, from whose mouth the heads of the people clearly heard the words of the Torah. The meaning of our verse is that Moses was the equivalent of a king, and the heads of the tribes were gathered unto him. This interpretation is supported by Scripture’s statement that the Torah was given to the kohanim , who, in my opinion, are meant by All His holy ones-they are in Thy hand (v. 3), and to all the elders of Israel (Deut. 31:9). This is what When the heads of the people were gathered refers to. Scripture also writes there, Assemble unto me all the elders of your tribes (Deut. 31:28). Rabbi Judah Ha-Levi, of blessed memory, says that the king alludes to the Torah. He similarly used to explain there was no king in Israel (Jud. 18:l).

LET REUBEN LIVE. Moses starts with the first-born, for this is the proper practice. He does not mention Simeon because of the incident of Baal-peor, for those who served Baalpeor were from the tribe of Simeon. Their number proves this. Also, their prince was killed. It is also possible that Moses followed in the footsteps of Jacob, who did not bless Simeon and Levi. The tribe of Levi was blessed out of respect for Aaron. Simeon had no one as great as Aaron. Should one who disputes argue, “Why did Moses bless Reuben?” The answer is that Jacob blessed Reuben. The blessing was have not thou the excellency (Gen. 49:4). The meaning of the latter is that Reuben shall be like one of his brothers. Moses mentions Judah after Reuben because he was in charge of a standard and he was the first to lead in battle. Next Levi and then Benjamin are mentioned because the Levites dwelled in Jerusalem, which was situated between Judah and Benjamin. Scripture clearly states this. Moses then mentions the tribe of Joseph so as not to delay naming him. He had already mentioned his younger brother. He next mentioned Zebulun because he waged war. He then mentioned Issachar. After Moses finished mentioning the children of the wives, he commenced with Gad, who camped among the standard of the children of the wives. Moses then mentions Dan, who was in charge of a standard. He then mentioned Naphtali because he was older than Asher.
LET REUBEN LIVE. A prayer.
AND NOT DIE. For it is possible that he will be as a person who lives a certain number of years and then dies.

IN THAT HIS MEN BECOME FEW. Ve-yehi metav mispar is to be rendered, and let his men not be numbered (few). It is similar to And I have not learned wisdom (Prov. 30:3) and to the bet of be-el shaddai (as God Almighty) (Ex. 6:3) as I have explained many times. Moses said this because it is possible for the tribe of Reuben to live forever but consist of few people. All things that are numbered are few. Compare, And I am men of number(Gen . 34:30).
AND THIS FOR JUDAH. He similarly said to Judah, “Let Judah live and not die.” He also added, “Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah” when he goes to war, because Judah would go into battle first.
AND BRING HIM IN UNTO HIS PEOPLE. To the camp, which was in Gilgal. On the other hand, it might be a prayer regarding those who go to do battle in the land of the enemy.

HIS HAND SHALL CONTEND FOR HIM. Rav lo (contend for him) means shall be sufficient for him so that he has no need for anyone to help him but God’s help alone. Others say that the word rav is related to the word merivah (conflict). The meaning of yadav rav lo is that his hands shall fight for him. Others say that the word rav is like the word rav (shot forth) in and He shot forth lightnings (Ps. 18:15). It is related to va-robbu (and shot at him) (Gen. 49:23).
AND OF LEVI. U-le-levi amar (and of Levi he said) is to be interpreted, And of Levi he said to God. Compare, say of me (li): He is my brother (Gen. 20:13).
WITH THY HOLY ONE. Le-ish chasidekha (with Thy holy one) means to the man who is Your holy one.

WHOM THOU DIDST PROVE AT MASSAH. Massah is a noun. It means a test. The meaning of our clause is: Aaron was pious. Aside from the incident at Meribah, for which You already punished him, no unseemly thing was found in him. Also, this verse supports my interpretation regarding the incident of the calf, that is, that Aaron made the calf for God’s glory.
[THY THUMMIM AND THY URIM.] This means may Thy Thummim and Thy Urim always be his and his seed’s.
WHO SAID. Moses speaks of the tribe. Samuel who came to the house of God as soon as he was weaned, to be trained in God’s service, is an example.
NOR KNEW HE HIS OWN CHILDREN. There were among them individuals who begot children for the service of God. FOR THEY HAVE OBSERVED

THY WORD, AND KEEP THY COVENANT. Compare, They kept (shameru) His testimonies , and the statue that He gave them (Ps. 99:7) so that they would teach them to Israel. Some say that the reference is to Whoso is on the Lord’s side, let him come unto me (Ex. 32:26).
THEY SHALL PUT INCENSE. The reference is to those among them who are kohanim .
AND WHOLE BURNT-OFFERING. Kalil (whole burnt offering) refers to the olah (burnt offering).
BLESS, LORD, HIS SUBSTANCE. The first-born and the tithe.
THE WORK OF HIS HANDS. The sacrifices.
SMITE THROUGH THE LOINS. Smite them that rise against him.
THAT THEY RISE NOT AGAIN. Min yekumun (that they rise not again) means of those that will rise against them. Compare, la-yam mekhassim (cover the sea) (Is. 11:9).
OF BENJAMIN HE SAID. Le-vinyamin means of Benjamin. Moses said of Benjamin, who is the beloved of the Lord, Benjamin shall dwell in safety by God, and God shall dwell between his shoulders.
HE COVERETH HIM. The reference is to God’s glory which, as Scripture writes, dwelled in Benjamin’s portion, in Jerusalem.

The meaning of between his shoulders is, in the center of his inheritance. Or between his shoulders means that God’s glory was visible. Furthermore, between his shoulders is also connected to covereth .
FOR THE PRECIOUS THINGS. Which the heavens will give.
THE FRUITS OF THE SUN. For the fruits of the seed and the vineyard are dependent upon the sun.

THE YIELD. Geresh (yield) is related to the word vayigreshu (cast up) in And its waters cast up (Is. 57:20). The moon does this via the moisture which is in the air, for its heat is unlike the power of the sun. Scripture reads moons because they renew themselves, and there are many of them in the year.
AND FOR THE TOPS. This means and for the precious things that grow on the tops of the ancient hills.
THE EVERLASTING HILLS. Scripture repeats itself.
AND FOR THE PRECIOUS THINGS OF THE EARTH. Scripture repeats itself. The earth refers to flat land.
AND THE FULNESS THEREOF. From what it is full of.
AND THE GOOD WILL OF HIM THAT DWELT IN THE BUSH. The reference is to heaven.

LET THE BLESSING COME. Tavotah (let the blessing come) refers to this blessing. Two signs, the tav and the heh , are joined together. Compare, ezratah (help) (Ps. 44:27); yeshu’atah (salvation) (Ps. 3:3); ba-tzaratah (in…distress) (Ps. 120:1). Moses compared the tribe of Joseph to a bullock because he earlier spoke of produce. Moses referred to Joseph as His firstling bullock (v. 17) because a first-born bullock has great strength as it is the first of its father’s might.
MAJESTY IS HIS. His body is large. It means that the tribe of Joseph is large in number.
THE HORNS OF THE WILD-OX. In power.
THE TEN THOUSANDS OF EPHRAIM. As in the words of Jacob.
REJOICE, ZEBULUN, IN THY GOING OUT. To war. Similarly Zebulun is a people that jeoparded their lives unto the death (Jud. 5:18).
IN THY TENTS. Compare, For he saw a resting-place that it was good (Gen. 49:15).

THEY SHALL CALL PEOPLES UNTO THE MOUNTAIN. Zebulun shall possess great wealth because he dwells where ships dock. This is the meaning of they shall suck the abundance of the seas . The word shefa (abundance) is related to the word shifat (caravan) in The caravan of camels shall cover thee (Is. 60:6).

AND THE HIDDEN TREASURES OF THE SAND. The word sefune (hidden) has no brother. It has the same meaning as temune (treasures). Similarly admat afar (dust). The meaning of the hidden treasures of the sand is that Zebulun will have so much wealth that they [the tribe] will hide it in the sand. And because of their wealth, they will come in a multitude to the mountain of God to offer sacrifices of thanksgiving to the Lord.
ENLARGETH GAD. Moses compares Gad to a lion. All who see him will flee from him. No one shall torment him.
AND HE CHOSE A FIRST PART FOR HIMSELF. This means he looked out for himself and sought an inheritance before the other Israelites.
FOR THERE A PORTION OF A RULER WAS RESERVED. The word chelkat (portion of) means a portion.
[A RULER.] Mechokek (ruler) refers to someone who is great and a ruler. Compare, My heart is toward the governors (le-chokeke) of Israel (Jud. 5:9).

[RESERVED.] The word safun (reserved) is similar to safun (ceiled) in and it is ceiled with cedar (Jer. 22:14); and sefunim (ceiled) in be-vattekhem sefunim (Haggai 1:4), which means your houses which are ceiled. The import of ki sham chelkak mechokek safun (for there a portion of a ruler was preserved) is that Gad saw the paneled palaces that were the portion of the nobles of the Amorites.
CAME. Va-yeta (came) is missing an alef . The meaning of our clause is that the heads of Gad came armed with the children of Israel. Moses prophetically saw this.

HE EXECUTED THE RIGHTEOUSNESS OF THE LORD. Gad fulfilled with his hands that which he spoke with his mouth, for the children of Gad vowed that they would go out with Israel to wage battle against their enemies. Moses did not mention Reuben. It is possible that he omitted Reuben because the tribe of Gad were greater warriors than the tribe of Reuben. The words of Chronicles, which states regarding the tribe of Gad, whose faces were like the faces of lions (I Chron. 12:9), is proof of this. We do not find this stated regarding the tribe of Reuben.
LEAPETH. The word yezannek (leapeth) has no companion in Scripture. Our clause is to be understood as follows: Moses compared Dan’s might to that of a lion’s whelp leaping from Mount Bashan.
SATISFIED WITH FAVOR. Seva ratzon (satisfied) is an adjective. It means he will be sated with favor.
THE SEA AND SOUTH. Yam ve-darom (the sea and south) means that Naphtali’s inheritance shall be in the southwest.
THE FAVORED. Ratzuy (favored) means the beloved.
AND LET HIM DIP HIS FOOT IN OIL. Because of the abundance of oil. It is similar to He washeth his garments in wine (Gen. 49:11). Jacob similarly said, his bread shall be fat (Gen. 49:20).
IRON AND BRASS SHALL BE THY BARS. For mountains of iron and brass shall be in his portion.

AND AS THY DAYS, SO SHALL THY STRENGTH BE. The word dovekha (thy strength) has no neighbor. The interpretation of the Aramaic translation is known, namely, that you will be strong all your days. Some say that the alef of dovekha is in place of the doubled letter. It is like the word baze’u (divide) in Whose land the rivers divide (Is. 18:2). They believe that dovekha is related to the word dovev (moving gently) in Moving gently the lips of those that are asleep (Cant. 7:10). This interpretation is not reasonable.
THERE IS NONE LIKE UNTO GOD, O JESHURUN. Moses goes back to bless all of Israel.
WHO RIDETH UPON THE HEAVEN. That is, who is mighty. The fact that He rideth upon the heaven is proof of this.
[AND IN HIS EXCELLENCY ON THE SKIES.] It means, the heavens stand by God’s might.

THE ETERNAL GOD IS A DWELLING-PLACE. Note that the word ma’on (dwelling-place) means a covering (i.e., a sukkah ). In Salem also is set His covering (sukko), And His dwelling-place (me’onato) in Zion (Ps. 76:3) is proof of this. There are many such examples. The meaning of our verse is: The eternal God is your covering. Compare, Even the Most High, thy habitation (me’onekha) (Ps. 91:9) and Thou hast been our dwelling-place (ma’on) (Ps. 90:1). The ma’on (dwelling place) is always above the one who takes refuge in it. The “place” is below.
AND UNDERNEATH ARE THE EVERLASTING ARMS. Which will support you.

Scripture reads everlasting to teach that it shall always be so. The hand will not weaken, and your covering ( ma’on ) will not be removed, for He is the eternal God. The meaning of kedem (everlasting) is that God has no beginning and no end. Scripture speaks in human terms when it speaks of beginning and end. The Gaon says that and underneath means and underneath God. He did not explain anything.
THE FOUNTAIN OF JACOB. All those who came forth out of the fountain of Jacob. Similarly And are come forth out of the fountain of Judah (Is. 48:1).
IN A LAND. El eretz is to be rendered, in a land. It is similar to if they pray in this place (el ha-makom ha-zeh) (I Kings 8:35).

YEA, HIS HEAVENS. The heavens of the earth or of Israel. The meaning of our verse is, it is the nature of the land to produce corn and oil. Also, the heavens shall always give their dew and there will be no need to water the ground.
WHO IS LIKE UNTO THEE. Among the nations.
THE SHIELD OF THY HELP. No evil shall come upon you.
AND THAT IS THE SWORD. He is the sword by which you will exalt yourself over all your enemies.
SHALT TREAD. Tidrokh (shall tread) is similar to midrakh (to tread on) in for the sole of the foot to tread on (Deut. 2:5). The contents of our verse are similar to the account of Gideon.

AND MOSES WENT UP. I believe that Joshua wrote from this verse onward, for Moses did not write after he ascended. Joshua wrote prophetically. And the Lord showed him; And the Lord said unto him (v. 4); and also, And he was buried (v. 6) are proof.
SO MOSES THE SERVANT OF THE LORD DIED THERE. Even in his death Moses, like a servant, did what God commanded him.

ACCORDING TO THE WORD OF THE LORD. For God told him, Get thee up (Deut. 32:49) and die (Deut. 32:50). Scripture similarly writes with regard to the death of Aaron, at the commandment of the Lord (Num. 33:38). It similarly states, At the commandment of the Lord they encamped (Num. 9:23).

AND HE WAS BURIED. Moses buried himself. He entered a cave in the valley. The same is true of but the shepherds fed them (otam), and fed not My sheep (Ezek. 34:8) and, And the officers of the children of Israel did see them (otam) (Ex. 5:19). Note, Mount Abarim is also known as Mount Nebo. Nebo is in the image of Mercury. Mount Abarim is also known as “the valley which is the top of Pisgah which is over against Beth-peor.” The fact that Scripture tells us that Israel journeyed from Bamoth to the valley that is in the field of Moab, by the top of Pisgah (Num. 21:20) is proof of this. Furthermore, Scripture writes, And Moses went up from the plains of Moab unto mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah (v. 1). Moses died there and his grave is there. Scripture states, So we abode in the valley over against Beth-peor (Deut. 3:29). Now, Scripture tells us that after Israel dwelt in the valley…the children of Israel journeyed, and pitched in the plains of Moab (Num. 22:1). Another verse states, And [Israel] pitched in the mountains of Abarim, in front of Nebo. And they journeyed from the mountains of Abarim, and pitched in the plains of Moab (Num. 33:47,48). Look, it is clear that Moses’ burial place was in the place where he died.
UNTO THIS DAY. These are the words of Joshua. He probably wrote this at the end of his days.

HIS NATURAL FORCE. The heh of lechoh (his natural force) is in place of a vav . It is like the heh of oholoh (his tent) (Gen. 9:21). Lechoh is related to the word lach (moist, fresh). Scripture notes this because old people are overtaken by dryness.
The word nas (abated) is the reverse of diffused.
THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL. However, when Aaron died, even all the house of Israel (Num. 20:29) mourned out of respect for Moses.
SO…WERE ENDED. When the days of weeping in the mourning of Moses were ended there, the children of Israel hearkened unto Joshua.

WAS FULL OF THE SPIRIT OF WISDOM. The reference is to the spirit of the Lord. For Moses had laid his hands upon him is proof of this, for there was not found in Israel one such as Joshua for Moses to lean on.
AND DID AS THE LORD COMMANDED MOSES. That they hearken unto Joshua.
FACE TO FACE. I have previously explained this.
THE MIGHTY HAND. The wonders at the sea.
THE GREAT TERROR. When Israel stood before Mount Sinai.
